summary: 15 concise trial-paper-only hypotheses distilled from the ResearchAgent run for ist3, grouped by per-hypothesis feature attribution.

mechanisms.description: Advanced age attenuates individualized benefit because pooled hierarchical CATE estimates from IST‑3 and meta‑analysis identify smaller Δ_i and lower Prob(NB>0) in older strata promoted by stability selection.

Adverse baseline CT imaging markers (low ASPECTS or hypodensity indicators) increase individualized sICH probability in the harm model and thereby reduce expected utility and net benefit for affected patients.

Higher pre‑morbid mRS reduces the individualized expected‑utility gain from alteplase because utility‑mapped TMLE estimates show smaller absolute improvements in 90‑day independence for patients with worse baseline function.
Concurrent antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment elevates individualized Δ_sICH_i in pooled harm models and mediates a reduction in net benefit despite similar estimated Δ_mRS for some patients.

Study‑level heterogeneity and trial epoch shift individualized Δ_i via hierarchical random effects, so that transportability analyses show different apparent benefit patterns between IST‑3 and later registry cohorts (e.g., pre‑EVT vs EVT‑era).

The joint posterior dependence between sICH occurrence and final 90‑day mRS explains part of the reduction in expected utility for some patients, such that joint modeling yields different NB estimates than assuming independence.

Patients with simultaneously high predicted Δ_mRS and high predicted Δ_sICH (from combined TMLE and Bayesian pipelines) represent preference‑sensitive cases where the clinician‑elicited w_sICH determines whether net benefit is positive.

Low effective sample size (ESS) regions in covariate space produce unstable individualized Δ_i that are pulled toward the pooled mean by hierarchical pooling, potentially masking true local benefit or harm mechanisms.

Time‑by‑age interactions detected in stability selection generate subgroups where the negative impact of delayed treatment on Δ_i is disproportionately larger in older patients, reducing individualized net benefit beyond additive expectations.

Patients rated as low‑benefit by the distilled interpretable rule nevertheless show residual TMLE posterior heterogeneity, implying that nonlinear combinations of covariates captured by the flexible ensemble drive subtle mechanisms of benefit absent from simple scores.

In registries with higher contemporary EVT availability, secular changes alter baseline control arm outcomes and thereby reduce observed Δ_i and recalibrate net‑benefit predictions relative to IST‑3 RCT‑based estimates, reflecting a mechanism of altered transportability.

Within the 6‑hour window, individualized absolute benefit (Δ_i) from alteplase decreases as onset‑to‑treatment time increases, consistent with HTE discovery and pooled CATE estimates showing smaller Δ_i for later treatment times.

An interaction between imaging (ASPECTS) and onset‑to‑treatment time creates strata in which very early treatment yields substantial Δ_expected_utility_mRS whereas delayed treatment in the same imaging strata increases Δ_sICH_i and flips net‑benefit thresholds.

Higher baseline NIHSS produces greater heterogeneity in Δ_i with some patients showing amplified absolute benefit yet concurrently higher individualized sICH risk according to the Bayesian harm model, creating a benefit–harm tradeoff in net‑benefit calculations.

Elevated baseline glucose and uncontrolled blood pressure act as effect modifiers by associating with both lower Δ_i and higher Δ_sICH_i in pooled models, leading to a reduced probability that net benefit exceeds zero.
